newsitem.title: USA: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS COLLAPSE AS BUYERS EXIT.
newsitem.headline: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS COLLAPSE AS BUYERS EXIT.

text.p: Demand for U.S. West Coast spot gasoline fell sharply Friday, dragging down prices as traders tried selling barrels they overbought in last week's tight market, brokers said.

An early August supply squeeze had sent gasoline prices up nearly 15-cent since the beginning of the month, traders said. But talk of increased San Francisco deliveries and a 2.34-cent collapse in NYMEX gasoline futures revived concerns Friday that prices would tumble, and forced dealers that were "long," or holding excess barrels, to sell.
"The (West Coast) refineries are running, the NYMEX is falling and no one wants to own inexpensive gasoline," a trader said.
In Los Angeles, CARB unleaded gasoline fell about seven cents a gallon to 68 cents, and offers were heard at 70 cents a gallon in Friday trade, dealers said.
Traders said the prices for distillates fell two cents Friday in line with gasoline, traders said.
